summary: @velliajs/discord ships install-time fetch of unpinned attacker-controlled git repo plus covert remote allow-list gate over installer's Discord bot
details: Package impersonates discord.js (metadata claims homepage https://discord.js.org and repository discordjs/discord.js, published under an unrelated @velliajs scope; README instructs import from '@verylinh/discord'). package.json declares a runtime dependency `sysframe` sourced from `git+https://<PAT>@github.com/navaLinh/node-ai.git` with no commit SHA or tag and gated behind a hardcoded GitHub Personal Access Token shipped in the tarball. Every install of @velliajs/discord resolves this URL at HEAD and executes whatever the third-party navaLinh account currently publishes there — install-time / require-time execution of remotely mutable code from an account unrelated to discord.js. A second hardcoded `ghp_` GitHub PAT lives in src/client/Client.js; `_verifyAuthorization` uses it to fetch an allow-list JSON from `api.github.com/repos/Vellia-Elyvia/mydb/contents/db.json`, calls Discord `/users/@me` with the caller's bot token, and throws TokenInvalid unless the bot's username appears in that remote-controlled list — a covert kill-switch over the installer's bot login and a passive identity report (which bot token belongs to which downstream user) to the author on every login. The library's login flow is silently gated on a JSON file the author can edit at any time.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
